newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jet prices rise with NYMEX, but diffs slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jet prices rise with NYMEX, but diffs slide.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel prices rose sharply in line with gains on NYMEX on Monday, despite a slump in differentials, industry sources said.
Prices firmed by about 1.50 cents a gallon, lifted by the continuing rally in heating oil, which is inspired by exports to Europe and already tight U.S. stocks.
As refiners tweak production of distillates up to meet the demand, other refined products are seeing a rise in stocks, whether the marketplace calls for it or not.
Last week, API pegged jet fuel output at 1.65 million barrels a day, nearly 200,000 bpd more than last year.
Stocks are 2.9 million over last year, API said.
"There's just a lot of jet production right now," said one U.S. Gulf Coast trader.

New York Harbor 54-grade jet was offered at about 0.15 to 0.35 cent over the November heating oil print, about 0.65 cent weaker than Friday's level. U.S. Gulf differentials slipped to about 1.75 cents under the screen.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
